text:
Review blocks approval because compaction now performs an interpret call for every record. Copying already typed fields requires ZERO inference, no classification booleans and no learned mapping. Keep the accepted requirements, manifest/cursor loops, original completeness guards, real bounded product visits, document write and root cleanup. Replace the four per-record classification transforms with direct existing foreach body.outputs object bindings from item fields. A record loop can have body.tasks=[] and outputs containing an object assembled from item.kind/item.tag/item.text/item.group/item.role etc.; no transform or value task is needed just to export typed fields. Keep nullable fields nullable. The global interpret tasks perform the business decisions using these observations, without preliminary classifier flags.
For initial consent/blockage, export only kind/tag/text/group/role, with NO href or selector. For global search selection, export the necessary observed link text/context/href and nullable role, with NO selector; avoid duplicating the same record text across separate inputs to the same consumer. For the visited product's field interpretation, export only necessary observed text/context; its URL/rank are already supplied explicitly, so do not copy every observed href/selector. Preserve nesting, order, duplicates, all records and original action data through existing source bindings. Global ranking/synthesis stays global. Do not substitute whole-collection extraction or per-record interpretation for deterministic projection.
The manifests currently request up to 200 records per page while the record loops allow 100. Narrow the producer request to 100 records per page so its declared page bound fits the existing loop bound; do not increase any limits. Keep manifest max 100 pages and max 3 product visits. Truncation must still fail before successful workbook creation. Preserve unrelated business work and the accepted interface.
